sources: dossier=Net position bullet 9 (agent dials proxy 'with the user's api-key') plus Required-behaviors bullet 'Anonymous-mode late-binding' (2026-06-08, corpus-bootstrap, artifact), corroborated independently by concept:host-agent-proxy's Invariants ('a well-known anonymous routing identity under which the anonymous-mode agent registers'); doc=host-agent.md 'What it is' stated api-key auth unconditionally, no mention of anonymous fallback; code=run.go:103-105 sets cfg.APIKey = AnonymousRoutingIdentity when empty, const defined run.go:31-32.
note: Anonymous registration is a real, dossier-and-corpus-corroborated agent behavior the doc omitted entirely. Added a clause to the 'What it is' authentication sentence.

sources: dossier=Required-behaviors bullets 'Loopback-only local HTTP listener' and 'Callback URL rewrite: the proxy rewrites callback_url ... before tunneling' (2026-05-24, artifact) establish the forward direction is child-originated callback traffic relayed toward the proxy; doc=host-agent.md 'What it is' said the agent 'serves ... local-HTTP-forward requests against locally-running binaries', implying agent-to-binary direction; code=local_http.go:20-58 localForwardHandler/forwardHTTP accept HTTP from the child on the agent's local listener and relay a ClientFrame_HttpForward upstream; run.go:305-306 returns the ServerFrame_HttpResponse.
note: The doc's phrasing inverted the direction of the fourth verb. Rewrote the sentence to state the agent relays child-raised local-HTTP callback requests on to the proxy, and dropped '/local-HTTP-forward' from the serve-against-binaries clause since it isn't a request served against the binary.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 'Trust posture is permissive by default ..., narrowed optionally by --allow-paths globs' (synthesized net position) and Intentional-absences bullet 'Capability/discovery config on the agent: deliberately stateless' (2026-05-24, artifact) together establish allow-paths as a real, distinct, optional boundary layered on top of the (still true) no-discovery invariant; doc=host-agent.md Invariants said only 'No capability config; the agent does not know in advance what binaries exist' with no mention of any path boundary anywhere in the doc; code=config.go:19 Config.AllowPaths, cmd/rimsky/cli/agent.go:54,66-68 populates it from --allow-paths, spawn.go:225-250 resolveBindingPath enforces it with the exact error text 'path %q not permitted by --allow-paths'.
note: The no-discovery invariant is correct but incomplete: it omits the optional allow-paths boundary the dossier treats as a first-class (if optional) trust control. Appended a clause naming it without contradicting the no-capability-config claim.

sources: dossier=silent on the specific resolution mechanism; design corpus=no other concept doc addresses shell vs. non-shell exec; doc=host-agent.md Invariants said 'absolute, relative, and bare-name paths all work via the shell search path'; code=spawn.go:60 SpawnService execs directly via exec.Command (no shell spawned) and spawnOnPickedPort builds cmd.Dir from params.Cwd (spawn.go:96-99); Go's exec.Command resolves a bare name via PATH lookup at construction time, an absolute path is used as-is, and a relative path resolves against cmd.Dir, not any search path.
note: This is not a contested design choice (no dossier or transcript ever proposed shelling out) — it is a plain mechanism misdescription in an otherwise-uncontested invariant (all three path forms working at exec time is undisputed). Corrected the mechanism description without changing the invariant's substance.

sources: dossier=Net position bullet 'The agent is stateless and configuration-free: ... no persistent state beyond auth. A restart loses in-flight spawn state; pre-restart spawn-ids are dead, detected by the proxy via connection state' establishes the intent is behavioral statelessness, not literal absence of any on-disk artifact; doc=host-agent.md Invariants said 'The agent has no persistent state of its own' unqualified; code=run.go:162-166,195-216 writeStatusFile writes a connection-status file on every connect and clears it on shutdown/disconnect, cmd/rimsky/cli/agent.go:132-136 writes a pid file for the CLI daemonizer; neither is read back by the agent to alter behavior.
note: Dossier intent (no state consulted across restarts) holds and is unchanged; the doc's literal wording was falsifiable by the informational status/pid markers. Qualified the claim to what the dossier actually means: no state that changes behavior across restarts.

sources: dossier=Required-behaviors 'Child contract' bullet ('the agent ... runs the Capabilities handshake per expected protocol before acking ready') and Net position bullet 12 (same, restated) both attribute the handshake to the agent, not the proxy (2026-05-24, artifact); doc=host-agent.md Boundaries said the binary 'advertises its own Capabilities via the proxy-driven handshake'; code=spawn.go:126-156,174-219 handleSpawn (agent-side) dials the child directly and calls handshakeCapabilities over that connection for each sp.GetExpectedProtocols() entry, returning bytes in SpawnAck.Capabilities — the proxy only supplies the expected-protocols list on the Spawn message, it does not participate in the handshake RPCs.
note: The doc misattributed which party drives the handshake. Reworded to credit the agent as the driver and note the proxy's role is limited to naming the expected protocols, matching the dossier's child-contract bullet.

sources: dossier=Required-behaviors 'Per-binding overrides' bullet: 'env vars, command args, working directory, ready/spawn-timeout on the Binding proto message, applied at exec; a binding with no overrides inherits env ...' (2026-06-06 + 2026-06-08, artifact) establishes per-binding env as a real override layered on inheritance; doc=host-agent.md Invariants said 'Spawned children inherit the agent's full environment' with no mention that binding-declared env can override an inherited name; code=spawn.go:154-157 env := os.Environ() then per-binding entries are appended afterward; Go's documented cmd.Env semantics (last occurrence of a duplicate key wins) make the appended binding entries win over inherited ones on name collision.
note: True but incomplete: the invariant presented inheritance as the whole story when the dossier's own per-binding-overrides promise means binding env silently wins on collision, including against PATH/loader vars. Added the override-on-collision clause.
